title: M&A announcement returns for acquirer firms

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

For this research question, an Event Study methodology is appropriate. The Event Study methodology is used to estimate the abnormal returns around an event (in this case, the M&A announcement). The key assumption is that the market model is correctly specified and that the abnormal returns are not influenced by other confounding events during the event window.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s13_data.csv")

# Filter the data for the event window [-1, +1]
event_window_data <- subset(data, event_day >= -1 & event_day <= 1)

# Calculate abnormal returns (AR) by subtracting the expected returns from the actual returns
event_window_data$ar <- event_window_data$ret - (event_window_data$beta * event_window_data$mkt_ret)

# Calculate the cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) for each stock
car <- aggregate(ar ~ stock_id, data = event_window_data, FUN = sum)

# Calculate the mean CAR across all stocks
mean_car <- mean(car$ar)

# Perform a t-test to check if the mean CAR is significantly different from zero
t_test_result <- t.test(car$ar, mu = 0)

# Print the mean CAR and the t-test result
cat("Mean CAR:", mean_car, "\n")
cat("t-test result:", t_test_result$p.value, "\n")

# Robustness check: Repeat the analysis excluding outliers (AR > 2 or AR < -2)
event_window_data_no_outliers <- subset(event_window_data, ar < 2 & ar > -2)
car_no_outliers <- aggregate(ar ~ stock_id, data = event_window_data_no_outliers, FUN = sum)
mean_car_no_outliers <- mean(car_no_outliers$ar)
t_test_result_no_outliers <- t.test(car_no_outliers$ar, mu = 0)

cat("Mean CAR (no outliers):", mean_car_no_outliers, "\n")
cat("t-test result (no outliers):", t_test_result_no_outliers$p.value, "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings

I expect the mean CAR to be negative, consistent with the acquirer's curse hypothesis. The magnitude of the CAR will depend on the specific data, but it should be statistically significant if the hypothesis holds true. The robustness check should provide similar results, indicating that the findings are not driven by outliers.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study with cross-sectional CAR regression; acquirer returns tested against zero
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Acquirers experience small negative CAR, consistent with overpayment hypothesis
